## Purpose

Language models do not read letters or words, they read tokens. This activity asks you to guess how many tokens six short strings split into (three about cake, three from biology), then shows the real split. Commit to a number before each reveal: the wrong guesses are the useful part. At the bottom of the page you can type your own words and see how they split.

It was built for the CAKE Coffee & Learn at CRUK CI sessions and works on its own for self-study.

::: {.callout-note}
## Which model are the tokens from?

Token counts come from OpenAI's GPT-4 tokeniser, **cl100k_base** (also used by GPT-3.5). Newer OpenAI models (GPT-4o onwards) use a different tokeniser, o200k_base, and Claude, Gemini and Llama each use their own. The same text can split into a different number of tokens depending on the model.
:::

## Notes

- The tokeniser is loaded from js-tiktoken 1.0.15 (`cl100k_base` ranks), a JavaScript port of OpenAI's tiktoken.
- Tokenisation runs in your browser. The page downloads the vocabulary (about 1 MB) once; nothing you type is sent anywhere.
- To compare tokenisers side by side, try [The Tokenizer Playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Xenova/the-tokenizer-playground) or [Tiktokenizer](https://tiktokenizer.vercel.app/).
